items.headline: Civil servants to get a 0.45-month mid-year bonus, with extra payouts for junior officers
items.summary: The Public Service Division said on 23 June that all civil servants will receive a mid-year Annual Variable Component of 0.45 months. Junior officers also get a one-time payment of S$250 to S$400, with the government citing first-quarter growth and a maintained 2.0-4.0% GDP forecast.

items.headline: Just 14% of Singapore workers are engaged at work, the lowest rate in the region
items.summary: A Gallup and Singapore Institute of Directors report launched on 22 June found only 14% of Singapore workers are engaged, below the 20% global and 25% South-east Asia averages. Disengagement is estimated to cost the economy about S$95 billion a year, with only 10% of under-35s feeling engaged.

items.headline: Household refuse collection fees to rise from 1 July in the first revision since 2024
items.summary: The National Environment Agency said monthly refuse fees for HDB and non-landed homes will rise S$0.44 to S$10.64, and landed-home fees S$1.50 to S$35.50, from 1 July. NEA attributed the increase to higher operating and manpower costs; HDB households can offset it with U-Save rebates.

items.headline: Driver jailed 32 weeks and fined S$6,000 over 73 mostly-staged traffic accidents
items.summary: A Singaporean driver was sentenced to 32 weeks' jail and a S$6,000 fine after being linked to 73 traffic accidents, most of them staged to claim insurance and cash payouts. The case is among the larger staged-accident frauds prosecuted in Singapore.

items.headline: Man, 59, jailed 12 weeks for exposing himself to a police officer after a Sembawang molestation
items.summary: Chandru Suryakanth, 59, was jailed 12 weeks after pleading guilty to sexual exposure and outrage of modesty. He molested a woman at a Sembawang supermarket in April 2025, then exposed himself to a 24-year-old female officer during a search at Woodlands police headquarters.

items.headline: George Kurian resigns as Union minister after his Rajya Sabha term ends, amid reshuffle buzz
items.summary: BJP leader George Kurian, Minister of State for Minority Affairs and for Fisheries, resigned on 23 June after his Rajya Sabha term ended on 21 June and the party declined to renominate him. President Murmu accepted the resignation on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's advice, ahead of a Cabinet meeting.

items.headline: Sensex sinks 893 points to 76,201 in its biggest June fall as weak data hits sentiment
items.summary: The BSE Sensex fell 893.39 points (1.16%) to 76,200.68 and the Nifty 50 dropped 278.80 points to 23,824.10 on 23 June, dragged by IT, metal and PSU bank stocks. Infosys, JSW Steel and Tata Consultancy Services led the losers as India VIX jumped about 8.6%.

items.headline: Vedanta slumps about 9% after a Rs 2,149-crore promoter block deal
items.summary: Vedanta shares fell as much as 8.77% to around Rs 279 on 23 June after promoter entity Twin Star Holdings sold roughly 7.3 crore shares, about 1.7% of equity, worth Rs 2,149 crore in a block deal at about Rs 292 a share. The sale stoked worries about a supply overhang.

items.headline: India's flash PMI eases to a three-month low as services growth slows to a 17-month low
items.summary: HSBC's flash India Composite PMI, compiled by S&P Global, fell to 57.4 in June from 59.3 in May, the lowest since March. The services index dropped to a 17-month low of 57.3 and manufacturing eased to 54.5, with hiring at its weakest in six months.

items.headline: Kerala High Court admits the state's appeal to overturn Dileep's acquittal in the 2017 actress assault case
items.summary: On 22 June a Kerala High Court division bench admitted the state government's appeal challenging the acquittal of actor Dileep and three others, and sought enhanced sentences for those convicted. A sessions court had acquitted Dileep, the alleged mastermind, in December 2025.

items.headline: Update: Streeting backs Burnham as Labour's leadership race opens, raising the prospect of a coronation
items.summary: Wes Streeting, seen as Andy Burnham's main rival, endorsed him after Keir Starmer announced his resignation, making a contested race less likely. Nominations open on 9 July and close a week later; if Burnham is unopposed he could become prime minister by about 17 July.

items.headline: Bank of England scraps individual stablecoin holding limits and sets a 40 billion pound issuance cap
items.summary: The Bank of England's final rules drop proposed caps of 20,000 pounds for individuals and 10 million pounds for firms, replacing them with a 40 billion pound issuance cap per systemic stablecoin. It also raised to 70% the share of backing assets that can be held in short-term government debt.

items.headline: Update: Met Office red extreme-heat warning takes effect as England and Wales near the all-time June record
items.summary: A rare red extreme-heat warning came into force for parts of central and southern England and Wales as a heat dome pushed temperatures toward records. The June high of 35.6C, set in 1976, was forecast to be broken, with long-standing records expected to fall by 25 June.

items.headline: Labour sets out its leadership timetable, with nominations opening on 9 July and a new leader by September
items.summary: Labour's ruling body set the succession process after Starmer's resignation: nominations open 9 July, contenders need the backing of 20% of Labour MPs, about 81, and a new leader is due before Parliament returns on 1 September. Starmer stays on as prime minister in the interim.

items.headline: US Senate passes the first war powers resolution to clear both chambers, seeking to halt the Iran campaign
items.summary: The Senate voted 50-48 on 23 June to pass a war powers resolution requiring congressional sign-off before further US military action against Iran. Four Republicans crossed over and one Democrat voted against; the White House dismissed its significance and a presidential veto is expected.

items.headline: EU hosts a Taliban delegation in Brussels for the first time in talks on Afghan deportations
items.summary: A five-member Taliban delegation met EU officials in Brussels on 23 June for closed-door talks on the return of failed Afghan asylum seekers, the first such hosting since the Taliban retook power. The Commission said it does not amount to recognition; rights groups condemned the meeting.

items.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian makes his first post-war foreign trip, to Pakistan
items.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian landed near Islamabad on 23 June, his first overseas trip since the February strikes, and was received by Pakistan's leadership. The visit thanked Islamabad for brokering the memorandum that framed a ceasefire and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: Lebanon and Israel resume US-mediated talks as a fragile Hezbollah ceasefire holds
items.summary: Lebanon resumed talks with Israel in Washington after President Joseph Aoun discussed a deconfliction mechanism with US Vice-President JD Vance and Qatar's prime minister. Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon continued even after a renewed ceasefire took effect; Hezbollah condemned the talks.

items.headline: South Africa sees deadly anti-migrant attacks and mass repatriations ahead of a 30 June deadline
items.summary: South African police investigated the murder of a Malawian man amid a wave of xenophobic violence, with more than 3,000 Malawians sheltering in a Durban field. Several governments have repatriated over 3,000 nationals before protest groups' 30 June deadline for foreigners to leave.

items.headline: Nvidia slips below a $5 trillion value as a chip-led selloff deepens on AI-spending worries
items.summary: A second day of tech selling on 23 June pushed Nvidia down about 3.4% and below a $5 trillion market value, while Micron fell roughly 11% ahead of earnings and SK Hynix and Samsung each dropped more than 12%. Investors questioned ballooning AI capital-spending plans.

items.headline: Menlo Ventures raises a record $3 billion on the back of its Anthropic bet
items.summary: Menlo Ventures announced $3 billion across two new funds on 23 June, its largest-ever raise, marking its 50th anniversary. The firm said its Anthropic stake, built on about $500 million invested, is now worth close to $14 billion as Anthropic's valuation tops $900 billion.

items.headline: A startup, Subquadratic, emerges from stealth claiming a breakthrough on the LLM attention bottleneck
items.summary: Miami-based Subquadratic unveiled SubQ, a model using a sparse-attention method it says runs far faster than current systems and handles a 12-million-token context. The firm reported running a benchmark for about $8 versus thousands for a leading rival, with an independent evaluation lending support.

items.headline: World-model startup Odyssey raises a $310 million round at a $1.45 billion valuation
items.summary: Odyssey, founded by Oliver Cameron and Jeff Hawke, closed a $310 million Series B led by Natural Capital at a $1.45 billion valuation, with Amazon, GV and AMD Ventures among backers. The world-model company also named AWS its preferred cloud provider.

items.headline: US Treasury issues a 60-day license letting Iran sell oil for the first time in 35 years
items.summary: The US Treasury issued a 60-day license authorising Iran to export and sell oil, fulfilling a provision of the war-ending memorandum after Tehran agreed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and readmit inspectors. It reopens access to Iranian crude for the first time in 35 years.

items.headline: Oil falls to a three-month low as the Iran sales waiver eases supply fears
items.summary: Brent crude fell to around $77 a barrel and WTI to about $73 on 23 June, the lowest in nearly three months, after Washington's 60-day license raised expectations of faster global supply. The drop extended losses from the prior session.

items.headline: South Korea's KOSPI crashes nearly 10%, triggering a circuit breaker as Samsung and SK Hynix dive
items.summary: The KOSPI plunged 9.99% to 8,203.84 on 23 June, halting trading for 20 minutes, after a regulator warning on single-stock leveraged ETFs spooked foreign investors. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell about 12% as overseas investors dumped a net 5.79 trillion won of shares.

items.headline: Wall Street sinks as a chip rout drives bets on a second Fed rate hike
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell about 2.2% and the S&P 500 dropped 1.4% on 23 June, led lower by semiconductors. Traders moved to price a second 25-basis-point rate increase by December under new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, a sharp shift from expectations of a cut weeks earlier.

items.headline: 🏎️ F1 heads to the Red Bull Ring for the Austrian GP with Antonelli leading the title race
items.summary: Formula 1 returns for round eight at the Red Bull Ring over 26-28 June. Kimi Antonelli leads the championship from George Russell, about 50 points back, with Lewis Hamilton resurgent after his first Ferrari win in Barcelona cut the gap to roughly 41 points.

items.headline: 🎾 Naomi Osaka beats Mertens to reach her first quarter-final of 2026 at Bad Homburg
items.summary: Naomi Osaka beat Elise Mertens 6-3, 6-3 in 67 minutes on the grass at Bad Homburg to reach her first WTA quarter-final of 2026. She struck seven aces and 22 winners in a tune-up the week before Wimbledon.

items.headline: 🏏 Australia thrash Pakistan to move to the brink of the Women's T20 World Cup semi-finals
items.summary: Australia posted 199 for 7 and restricted an already-eliminated Pakistan well short at Headingley on 23 June, extending their unbeaten run at the Women's T20 World Cup. The win moves the defending side to the verge of a semi-final place in Group 1.

items.headline: 🏏 Athapaththu century revives Sri Lanka's Women's T20 World Cup semi-final hopes
items.summary: Captain Chamari Athapaththu struck a century as Sri Lanka beat Ireland in their Group 2 match on 23 June, keeping their semi-final qualification alive at the England-hosted Women's T20 World Cup.

items.headline: 🎾 Grigor Dimitrov notches his 50th career grass-court win in his Mallorca opener
items.summary: Grigor Dimitrov beat Marc Polmans 6-1, 7-6(3) at the Mallorca Championships on 23 June for his 50th tour-level win on grass. The Bulgarian called it a reminder he is still competitive as he builds toward Wimbledon.

items.headline: The first ticking 'nuclear clocks' arrive, promising timekeeping beyond today's best atomic clocks
items.summary: Two research teams, one in Europe and one in China, built the first working nuclear clocks, which keep time using energy transitions in the nucleus of thorium-229 rather than in electrons. The devices could eventually outperform optical clocks and aid searches for dark matter and new physics.

items.headline: NASA's upgraded Cold Atom Lab makes quantum matter five times larger aboard the space station
items.summary: Astronauts powered up NASA's upgraded Cold Atom Lab on the International Space Station, which chills atoms to near absolute zero to form Bose-Einstein condensates now up to five times larger than before. The new modules enable longer microgravity observations for fundamental-physics tests.

items.headline: ESA's Euclid mission releases a deep new survey of the Milky Way's inner bulge
items.summary: ESA published Euclid's second quick data release on 24 June, the Euclid Galactic Bulge Survey, a deep, wide-field view of nine adjoining fields near the galactic centre imaged in about 24 hours. The data is aimed at hunting exoplanets via microlensing ahead of a full release in October.

items.headline: Stem-cell transplants put a severe spinal-cord and optic-nerve autoimmune disease into 15-year remission
items.summary: Researchers reported that a man and a woman with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, which damages the spinal cord and optic nerve, have remained in remission for more than 15 years after stem-cell transplants. The cases point to a potential durable treatment for the rare condition.

fun_fact.headline: Mauna Kea is Earth's tallest mountain measured base to summit
fun_fact.body: Measured from base to summit rather than from sea level, the tallest mountain on Earth is Hawaii’s Mauna Kea, which rises about 10,210 metres from its base on the Pacific seafloor. That far exceeds Mount Everest’s 8,849 metres above sea level — Everest is the highest point above the sea, but not the tallest mountain measured base to peak.

puzzle.title: The Unfolded Cube
puzzle.body:
The six faces of a cube are shown unfolded below as letters A–F.

Row 1:  .  A  .  .
Row 2:  B  C  D  E
Row 3:  .  F  .  .

(A sits above C; B, C, D, E run left to right; F sits below C.)

When the net is folded back into a cube, which face is opposite B, and which face is opposite A?
puzzle.approach: Pick one square as the front face and mentally fold the others up around it.
puzzle.answer:
B is opposite D, and A is opposite F.

Take C as the front face. B (left of C) becomes the left face and D (right of C) becomes the right face, so B and D are opposite. A (above C) becomes the top and F (below C) becomes the bottom, so A and F are opposite. E, two squares along the row, wraps around to the back, making C and E the last opposite pair.

word_puzzle.title: Adding Up
word_puzzle.body:
Rearrange all the letters of the phrase below to form a different common arithmetic phrase.

ELEVEN PLUS TWO

Hint: the two phrases are not only anagrams of each other — they are also numerically equal.
word_puzzle.approach: Count the letters first, then look for another arithmetic phrase that uses exactly the same ones.
word_puzzle.answer:
TWELVE PLUS ONE.

Both phrases use exactly the same thirteen letters — three E’s, two L’s, and one each of V, N, P, U, S, T, W and O. Fittingly, eleven plus two and twelve plus one both equal thirteen.
